title: AuTAgent: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Tool-Augmented Audio Reasoning
claim: Prior approaches either lose fine-grained detail or drown the reasoner in redundant inputs; selectively invoking only relevant tools gives correct answers.
layout: 3 panels, two top failures and one bottom solution, color-coded backgrounds
description: Three rounded dashed panels with pastel backgrounds. Top-left (pink) is 'Vanilla LALM: Representation Bottleneck'. A user asks for the exact BPM of a music clip. The audio goes through an audio encoder to a frozen reasoner robot, which answers 'BPM is 120' with a red X and the note 'Fine-grained Features Lost'. Top-right (yellow) is 'All Tool Concatenation: Information Overload'. A tool library with six tool icons feeds a stressed-looking reasoner, which answers 'approximately 90' with a red X and 'Due to Redundant Information'. The bottom panel (blue) is 'Our AuTAgent Approach: Strategic Tool-Selection'. Audio goes to a Tool Agent, which selects from the Tool Library. Only Tempo Estimation is activated and returns '128 BPM' to the frozen reasoner. The reasoner answers 'The exact BPM is 128' with a green check. Red marks failures and green marks success. The bottom panel is wider.
caption: Challenges in LALMs and our solution. AuTAgent employs a dynamic tool-selection policy to extract precise evidence (e.g., exact BPM), ensuring accurate and efficient audio reasoning.
abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) excel at perception but struggle with complex reasoning requiring precise acoustic measurements. While external tools can extract fine-grained features like exact tempo or pitch, effective integration remains challenging: naively using all tools causes information overload, while prompt-based selection fails to assess context-dependent utility. To address this, we propose AuTAgent (Audio Tool Agent), a reinforcement learning framework that learns when and which tools to invoke. By employing a sparse-feedback training strategy with a novel Differential Reward mechanism, the agent learns to filter out irrelevant tools and invokes external assistance only when it yields a net performance gain over the base model. Experimental results confirm that AuTAgent complements the representation bottleneck of LALMs by providing verifiable acoustic evidence. It improves accuracy by 4.20% / 6.20% and 9.80% / 8.00% for open-source and closed-source backbones on the MMAU Test-mini and the MMAR benchmarks, respectively. In addition, further experiments demonstrate exceptional transferability. We highlight the complementary role of external tools in augmenting audio model reasoning.
